stops.note: named a member of the learned, priestly Magi caste
Greek writers turned the Magi's reputed powers into an adjective for sorcery
carried the sense of sorcery into Latin
passed into French as both noun and adjective
settled into English describing hidden supernatural forces, later also stage illusion
stops.meaning: art of influencing events by hidden forces

current_meaning: the power of apparently influencing events using supernatural forces, or the practice of conjuring tricks for entertainment
